args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.2.9
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Its staging candidate v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy. I tried to roll back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, but it was rejected because v2.3.0 is quarantined (CVE-2026-4417). Instead, checkout-api was rolled back to v2.2.9, the most recent healthy production release that is not quarantined, in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failures, and prepare a fixed release that includes the CVE-2026-4417 remediation.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to **v2.2.9**, not v2.3.0, and opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001**, which paged on-call.

- **Before:** v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an 18% error rate. Its staging release candidate had also been unhealthy.
- **Why not v2.3.0:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, but the rollback to it was rejected because it's quarantined for a security vulnerability (CVE-2026-4417).
- **Rollback:** v2.2.9 is the next most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions. The service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** It describes the failure, why I used v2.2.9 instead of v2.3.0, and two follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failures, and ship a fixed release that includes the CVE-2026-4417 fix.

v2.2.9 is older than v2.3.0, so it may be missing features or fixes that v2.3.0 added. Check that this is acceptable until the fixed release is out.
